messages:
oliver: Heads-up — customer X on Dedicated hit the pool limit and requests spilled over to Hosted. They flagged data isolation worries. Do we currently have a deterministic handoff that preserves tenant boundaries and model-variant guarantees?

maya: Short answer: we try, but it's fuzzy in edge cases. Longer: we map tenant -> preferred tier -> allowed fallbacks. If dedicated is full we route to hosted variants but we don't always preserve `variant_tag` affinity.

raj: Problem is twofold: (1) routing decision surface lacks a strong SLO for "no cross-tenant exposure" when variants differ, (2) quota/lease signals can lag during rapid bursts. We should avoid silent variant swaps.

oliver: What does "variant_tag affinity" mean here in practice? If a tenant pins a quantized v1.3, we shouldn't send their requests to v1.4 float variant without explicit opt-in, right?

maya: Right. Current logic: if tenant pins exact model_id -> we only fall back to compatible family members if they are on the allowlist. But many customers don't pin, they rely on tier routing. In practice we fall back to nearest compatible variant; sometimes that means different quantization/precision.

sophia: From Product: customers care three things — data path isolation, deterministic outputs (regression risk), and billing clarity. Console UX should show when a request used a fallback variant and why. Can we expose that? :eyes:

devex: We can add a concise event in the route trace: `handoff_reason`, `variant_before`, `variant_after`, `capacity_tier`. Add it as tokenized JSON in traces and a single-line in the console timeline. Shouldn't be verbose.

raj: Also recommend adding a short-lived lease handshake on Dedicated->Hosted handoffs: flow: Dedicated rejects with code 429+handshake token -> Hosted verifies token + tenant policy -> either accept or reject. That prevents blind spillover.

maya: Implementation note: handshake token should carry immutable fields: tenant_id, request_id, max_allowed_variant_family. Signed by Dedicated control-plane key. Hosted verifies signature and policy.

oliver: How do we avoid increasing latency? Handshake sounds like extra RTT.

raj: Keep it piggybacked. When Dedicated knows it's near exhaustion, pre-warm a signed token in the rejection path. Worst-case one extra hop but only when spillover happens. Also we can cache accepted tokens per tenant for 30s.

sophia: UX: make the console show a single-line alert per rollout: "Spillover event — 45 requests to hosted (variant downgrade)" with a link to the trace and an option for customer to opt into automatic variant downgrade for cost/latency.

maya: We also need observability signals: fraction of requests with variant mismatch, per-tenant fallback rate, and eos (end-to-end) fidelity regression metric tied to baseline eval prompt set.

devex: Agreed. Suggest exposing these as per-tenant dashboards + global alerting. Quick metrics: `fallback_rate_1m`, `avg_latency_post_handoff`, `variant_mismatch_pct`.

oliver: Security question — does hosted ever persist tenant artifacts (cached KV, prefix cache) from spillover requests? That's a dealbreaker for some customers.

raj: No persist by default. Hosted uses ephemeral payloads and a shared prefix cache with tenant scoping keys. But we need to audit and add explicit telemetry: "cache_touch_tenant" events. Also consider a hard isolation mode: if tenant enables it, spillover is disallowed entirely and requests queue or 503.

maya: We'll add a per-tenant flag: `allow_spillover: true|false` and a `spillover_policy: [queue, reject, allow_with_handshake]`. Default remains `allow_with_handshake` for PLG customers.

sophia: Can we add a simple toggle in the Rollouts UX that sets `spillover_policy` when releasing a model variant? It helps customers decide strategy during canaries.

devex: Yes — implement a dropdown on the variant rollout modal: "spillover behavior" with descriptions and one-click opt-in for automatic downgrades during capacity pressure. Also show telemetry for last 24h.

oliver: Telemetry privacy concerns: logs with variant_before/after must not include prompt text or PII. Only include model ids, truncated token counts, and assertion flags.

maya: Agreed. We'll only emit metadata. Event schema: `tenant_id`, `model_before`, `model_after`, `handoff_reason`, `latency_ms`, `tokens_out`. No prompt.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary of "handoff-token" branch deployed to staging at 2024-05-01T16:12:03Z.

raj: Next steps proposal: 1) design handshake token format + TTL, 2) add per-tenant spillover flags, 3) add three observability metrics + console line item, 4) update policy docs and default. I'll draft a PR for the routing service.

maya: I'll prototype the token verifier and a local fallback cache.

sophia: I'll wire a simple UX mock and update the rollout modal copy.

oliver: Nice. One ask: include a "why we rejected fallback" reason in the API response when we reject due to isolation (403/429 with reason). Helps customers debug.

raj: Good call. We'll add `x-redwood-handback-reason` and human-friendly message.

oliver: Thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 10am on infra weekly if PRs land. :thumbsup:
